setting.time_period: Mid-18th century, year of grace 17--, age of sail and piracy after Captain Flint
setting.world: Historical real-world maritime Britain and Caribbean
setting.description: Rural west England around the lonely Admiral Benbow Inn at Black Hill Cove, the bustling docks and taverns of Bristol, aboard the 200-ton schooner Hispaniola at sea, and a remote uninhabited Treasure Island in southern waters with gray woods, sandy spits, marshes, hills including the Spy-glass, Skeleton Island, a log-house stockade with palisade, Ben Gunn's cave, and north and south anchorages.

characters.name: Jim Hawkins
characters.physical_description: A young boy with a fresh youthful face. Wears simple plain country clothes of an inn-boy, including a jacket with pockets and a sea cap.

characters.name: Billy Bones
characters.physical_description: A tall, strong, heavy nut-brown man with a tarry pigtail over his soiled blue coat. Has ragged scarred hands with black broken nails and a dirty livid-white saber cut across one cheek, wearing a cocked hat and carrying a brass telescope and cutlass.

characters.name: Doctor Livesey
characters.physical_description: A neat bright man with powder-white hair worn in a wig and bright black eyes. Of trim build, dressed as a gentleman in 18th-century coat with a pleasant clean-shaven face.

characters.name: Squire Trelawney
characters.physical_description: A tall man over six feet high, broad in proportion, with a bluff roughened reddened lined face. Has very black eyebrows, dressed as a gentleman.

characters.name: Long John Silver
characters.physical_description: A very tall and strong man with a big plain pale intelligent face as big as a ham and fair skin. His left leg is cut off close by the hip, using a crutch under his left shoulder, typically wearing an old cocked hat, immense blue coat with brass buttons, and carrying a parrot on his shoulder.

characters.name: Black Dog
characters.physical_description: A pale tallowy creature wanting two fingers of the left hand. Wears a cutlass, with a not very fighter-like yet seafaring look.

characters.name: Pew
characters.physical_description: A dreadful hunched blind man wearing a great green shade over eyes and nose and a huge old tattered sea-cloak with a hood. Taps before him with a stick, appearing positively deformed.

characters.name: Captain Flint
characters.physical_description: A notorious buccaneer captain known only by reputation and described as blue-faced in death. No living appearance described, associated with a blue scarf about the head when dying.

characters.name: Captain Flint Parrot
characters.physical_description: A small green parrot with bright plumage kept in a cage in the galley. Perches on Long John's shoulder, with a sharp beak and vivid feathers.

characters.name: Captain Smollett
characters.physical_description: A sharp-looking man with a stern tight-mouthed face. Dressed as a ship's master in seaman's clothing, of sturdy build.

characters.name: Mr. Arrow
characters.physical_description: A brown old sailor with earrings in his ears and a squint. Dressed as a ship's mate.

characters.name: Job Anderson
characters.physical_description: A powerfully built seaman serving as boatswain, with a loud commanding presence. Dressed in common sailor clothes.

characters.name: Israel Hands
characters.physical_description: A careful wily old experienced seaman with grizzled hair and frayed ringlet whiskers, brandy-faced and tanned. Wears common sailor clothes.

characters.name: Ben Gunn
characters.physical_description: A white man burned dark by the sun with blackened lips and startling fair eyes. Clothed in tatters of old ships' canvas and sea-cloth patched with brass buttons and sticks, wearing an old brass-buckled leather belt, goatskins.

characters.name: Tom Redruth
characters.physical_description: An elderly sullen gamekeeper, oldest of the party, over six feet high. Has a weathered aged face, dressed in gamekeeper's country clothes.

characters.name: Richard Joyce
characters.physical_description: A pleasant polite man serving as valet, of neat tidy appearance. Dressed as a manservant in livery-like clothes.

characters.name: John Hunter
characters.physical_description: A steady sturdy manservant of middle stature. Dressed as a manservant in plain servant's clothes.

characters.name: Abraham Gray
characters.physical_description: A stout able seaman with a plain honest face. Dressed in forecastle sailor clothes.

characters.name: Tom Morgan
characters.physical_description: An old gray-haired mahogany-faced sailor with a rolling quid in his cheek. Dressed in worn sailor clothes.

characters.name: George Merry
characters.physical_description: A long ill-looking man of five-and-thirty with yellow eyes. Dressed in soiled sailor clothes.

characters.name: Dick Johnson
characters.physical_description: A young seaman, youngest hand, with a youthful ordinary face. Dressed in common sailor clothes.

characters.name: O'Brien
characters.physical_description: A young though very bald Irish seaman. Wears a red nightcap and common sailor clothes.

characters.name: Supervisor Dance
characters.physical_description: A mounted officer of His Majesty's revenue, straight and stiff in bearing. Dressed in riding coat as a revenue officer.

characters.name: Mrs. Hawkins
characters.physical_description: A middle-aged country inn-woman with a careworn face. Wears plain widow-like working clothes, apron and cap.

chapters.title: I
chapters.summary: Young Jim Hawkins recalls how the scarred Captain Billy Bones took lodging at his father's Admiral Benbow Inn, paying in gold and watching the coast for seafaring men while bribing Jim to watch for a one-legged man. The captain terrorizes the parlor with drunken songs and dreadful pirate stories, stays on long unpaid until he hastens Jim's father's decline, until Doctor Livesey confronts and cows him at knifepoint.
chapters.cover_description: A tall scarred nut-brown seaman with a saber cut, tarry pigtail, soiled blue coat and cocked hat stands at the door of the lonely Admiral Benbow Inn beside his great sea-chest on a handbarrow, looking over the cove while a boy watches.

chapters.title: II
chapters.summary: On a bitter winter morning a pale stranger missing two fingers, Black Dog, ambushes the inn to confront Billy Bones, his old shipmate. Their rum talk over the captain's past erupts into a cutlass fight that leaves Black Dog wounded and fleeing and the captain collapsed with a stroke. Doctor Livesey bleeds the captain back to consciousness and warns that more rum means death.
chapters.cover_description: Billy Bones in a soiled blue coat swinging his cutlass to slash the wooden Admiral Benbow inn signboard on a frosty winter morning, while the pale wounded Black Dog flees bleeding down the road, breath hanging in the cold air.

chapters.title: III
chapters.summary: The sick Billy Bones begs Jim for rum and confesses he was Flint's first mate, warning Jim to watch for the black spot and a one-legged man and to fetch help when they come. Jim's father dies suddenly, and in the gloomy mourning days the weakened captain drinks and wanders the inn until a blind beggar forces Jim to lead him to Bill to deliver the black spot marked ten o'clock, after which the captain collapses dead of apoplexy.
chapters.cover_description: A dreadful hunched blind beggar in a green shade and tattered sea-cloak gripping a terrified inn-boy's hand on a foggy road outside a country inn, tapping with a stick.

chapters.title: IV
chapters.summary: Terrified to stay alone with Billy Bones's corpse, Jim and his mother brave the fog to seek help in the hamlet, but the villagers fear Captain Flint too much to defend the inn. The mother shames them into giving a pistol and fetching the doctor, then returns with Jim to open the captain's chest to claim her dues before his shipmates return.
chapters.cover_description: A widowed innkeeper woman counting gold coins from a dead sea captain's open chest by candlelight while her young son holds a cloth bag, with fog and full moonlight outside the Admiral Benbow inn.

chapters.title: V
chapters.summary: Jim watches Pew lead seven or eight pirates to storm the Admiral Benbow, only to find Billy Bones dead and his chest already rifled. As the crew quarrels over the missing Flint papers, revenue officers gallop in, scattering the pirates and trampling the abandoned Pew to death. Rescued by Supervisor Dance, Jim returns to the smashed inn and reveals he carries the sought-after packet, riding behind Dogger to put it in Doctor Livesey's safety.
chapters.cover_description: Blind Pew in tattered sea-cloak and green eye-shade, stick raised, screaming on a moonlit country road as four galloping revenue horses trample him outside the Admiral Benbow Inn at night.

chapters.title: VI
chapters.summary: Jim Hawkins rides hard with Supervisor Dance to find Doctor Livesey, ending at Squire Trelawney's Hall library where he delivers Billy Bones's oilskin packet. Doctor Livesey and the squire examine the captain's account-book of plunder and the thimble-sealed treasure map of Flint's island with three red crosses. Thrilled, Trelawney resolves to fit out a ship at Bristol with Jim as cabin-boy, while Livesey extracts a vow of absolute silence until they are at sea.
chapters.cover_description: A grand 18th-century library at night lit by a bright fireplace, where a tall squire and a wigged doctor lean over a table examining a treasure map with red crosses, while a boy in country clothes watches beside a half-eaten pigeon pie.

chapters.title: VII
chapters.summary: While kept at the Hall under Redruth's charge, Jim dreams over the treasure map until the squire's letter from Bristol announces the bought schooner Hispaniola and the hiring of cook Long John Silver and a crew. Jim and Redruth visit his mother at the repaired Admiral Benbow, bid a tearful farewell, travel by night mail-coach to Bristol, and meet the squire on the bustling quays to learn they sail for treasure tomorrow.
chapters.cover_description: Young Jim Hawkins on the crowded Bristol quays at dawn among towering tall ships, sailors aloft on rigging and singing at work, tarry docks and carved figureheads, meeting the beaming Squire Trelawney dressed like a sea officer in stout blue cloth.

chapters.title: VIII
chapters.summary: Jim is sent to find John Silver at the Spy-glass tavern, where he is charmed by the cheerful one-legged landlord despite spotting Black Dog there. Silver stages an outraged pursuit of Black Dog and pleads his helplessness so cleverly that Jim vouches for his innocence. Silver then reports the affair to Squire Trelawney and Doctor Livesey, winning their complete trust.
chapters.cover_description: Long John Silver, a towering one-legged sea-cook with crutch under shoulder, whistling cheerfully among tables in the bright clean Spy-glass tavern with its brass telescope sign, red curtains and tobacco smoke.

chapters.title: IX
chapters.summary: Jim and his party board the Hispaniola where Captain Smollett bluntly declares he distrusts the cruise, the crew, and his mate. Smollett reveals the treasure secret and island position have been blabbed to all hands and demands powder and arms be moved aft and the map kept secret. The squire angrily yields and the crew rebuilds the stern into a garrison, while Silver questions the change and the captain coldly rebuffs Jim.
chapters.cover_description: The Hispaniola at anchor as a rowboat pulls alongside, with stern Captain Smollett confronting Squire Trelawney and Doctor Livesey in the cramped cabin while Jim Hawkins looks on.

chapters.title: X
chapters.summary: The Hispaniola sails from Bristol with Silver leading a shanty, and the voyage proves prosperous except for mate Mr. Arrow drinking himself overboard and being replaced by Job Anderson. Jim befriends cook Long John Silver in his spotless galley while Squire Trelawney and Captain Smollett feud over a spoiled, grog-filled crew and the fateful apple barrel. On the last night outward, Jim hides inside the empty apple barrel and overhears Silver, realizing all honest lives aboard depend on what he le
chapters.cover_description: Young Jim Hawkins curled hidden inside a wooden apple barrel on the dark deck of the Hispaniola at sundown, listening in terror as one-legged cook Long John Silver leans against the barrel, with the moonlit sea and sails behind them.

chapters.title: XI
chapters.summary: Hidden in the apple barrel, Jim overhears Long John Silver corrupting young Dick Johnson with pirate lore and promises of fortune. Silver and Israel Hands then debate the mutiny, Silver insisting they wait until Captain Smollett has sailed them to the island and Livesey and Trelawney have found the treasure, before killing the honest party. Jim narrowly escapes discovery, learns some faithful men remain, and hears the cry of Land ho! under moonlight.
chapters.cover_description: A moonlit night on the deck of the sailing ship Hispaniola, a terrified boy crouched hidden inside a large open apple barrel among apples, overhearing the one-legged ship's cook Long John Silver on his crutch talking to seamen beside the barrel, silver moonlight on the masts and foresail.

chapters.title: XII
chapters.summary: The Hispaniola sights the treasure island under moonlight as fog lifts, and Silver smoothly identifies it as Skeleton Island while hiding his disappointment at the altered chart without treasure marks. Still horrified from overhearing the mutiny plot, Jim secretly warns Livesey, luring the officers below with a grog ruse, where he reveals Silver's plan and they realize they have only seven reliable men against nineteen mutineers.
chapters.cover_description: Moonlit night on the deck of the Hispaniola, crew crowded at the weather bow staring southwest as fog lifts to reveal a distant island with two low conical hills and a higher cloud-capped peak behind, moon shining on the sea wake.

chapters.title: XIII
chapters.summary: The Hispaniola arrives becalmed off gloomy Treasure Island and must warp by boat into a silent, landlocked, fever-smelling haven behind Skeleton Island. Discipline collapses as the crew growls toward open mutiny, with only Long John Silver able to soothe them. To buy time the officers grant an afternoon ashore, and Jim impulsively stows away in a boat and flees alone into the island thicket.
chapters.cover_description: The Hispaniola rolling becalmed under bright morning sun off the grey melancholy woods and wild naked rock spires of Treasure Island, dominated by the sheer pedestal-like Spy-glass peak, with yellow sand-breaks, foaming surf, pines, and crying seabirds

chapters.title: XIV
chapters.summary: Jim slips away from Silver to explore the island but overhears Silver trying to recruit the honest sailor Tom to the mutiny. After a distant death-cry signals Alan's murder, Tom defies Silver and is brutally struck down with Silver's crutch and stabbed to death as Jim watches hidden. Terrified he will be discovered next, Jim flees in panic toward the pine woods at the foot of the twin-peaked hill.
chapters.cover_description: Long John Silver standing over the motionless body of Tom in a sunlit green dell beside the steaming marsh, calmly wiping his bloodstained knife on a whisp of grass with his crutch under his arm and hat back on his head, while Jim watches hidden in the live-oak thicket.

chapters.title: XV
chapters.summary: Fleeing the mutineers, Jim encounters a wild white man who proves to be Ben Gunn, marooned three years on the island and desperate for Christian food. Gunn claims to be rich and promises to help Jim's party for a thousand pounds and passage home, recounting Flint's burial of the treasure and his own marooning. Their talk is interrupted by cannon fire from the ships, and they run toward the Union Jack flying over the stockade.
chapters.cover_description: A sun-blackened ragged castaway in patchwork canvas and goatskins kneeling in supplication before a boy in the pine woods of a tropical island, with the Union Jack distant over the trees.

chapters.title: XVI
chapters.summary: With the Hispaniola wind-bound and Jim Hawkins gone ashore with the mutineers, the doctor scouts the island and finds the defensible stockade with fresh water. The loyal party races to provision the blockhouse, ferrying arms, food, and medicine ashore under threat to the mutineers left aboard. They then abandon the ship entirely, dumping spare weapons overboard and escaping with the defecting Abraham Gray as the tide ebbs.
chapters.cover_description: Doctor Livesey discovering the abandoned log-house stockade enclosing a clear spring on a knoll, with its six-foot palisade and loopholed walls standing empty in the tropical heat.

chapters.title: XVII
chapters.summary: On the fifth and final jolly-boat trip, the doctor's overloaded party is swept westward by the ebb away from the stockade landing and exposed to the Hispaniola's long nine cannon. Trelawney fires and downs one pirate but cannot stop the race for the beach as the pirates launch their gigs. At the cannon's discharge the captain backs water and the jolly-boat sinks in shallow water, leaving the men soaked with most powder, provisions, and guns lost as they wade ashore fearing for Hunter and Joyce.
chapters.cover_description: An overloaded wooden jolly-boat sinking by the stern in three feet of clear water near a sandy beach, five soaked men wading ashore clutching guns overhead while a distant ship fires a long nine cannon with a puff of smoke.

chapters.title: XVIII
chapters.summary: The doctor's party outruns the mutineers to the stockade and wins the first firefight, but Tom Redruth is mortally wounded by a shot from the bush and dies in the log-house. Captain Smollett raises British colors, counts critically short rations, endures an evening cannonade without striking the flag, loses the stranded pork to Silver's men, and is interrupted by Jim Hawkins climbing alive over the stockade.
chapters.cover_description: Defenders hoist the British flag over a rough log-house inside a timber stockade while cannonballs from the anchored ship sail overhead and bury in the sand, with weary men in 18th-century dress watching from the enclosure.

chapters.title: XIX
chapters.summary: Jim learns Ben Gunn believes friends hold the stockade under the Union Jack and begs for a secret meeting with a gentleman on his word of honor. After an hour-long cannonade from the Hispaniola flying the Jolly Roger, Jim rejoins the faithful party in the crude, sand-blown log-house where Tom Redruth lies dead. Smollett organizes watches, burial, and a plan to whittle down the mutineers, until Jim is awakened by Silver approaching under a flag of truce.
chapters.cover_description: Jim Hawkins crouching among shore-side trees at sunset watching the Hispaniola flying the black Jolly Roger while a cannon flash fires and mutineers burn the jolly-boat on the beach.

chapters.title: XX
chapters.summary: Silver comes under a flag of truce to demand the treasure chart in exchange for sparing the stockade party's lives and offering rescue or passage. Captain Smollett coldly refuses to bargain or betray Gray and orders the mutineers to surrender unarmed for trial in England. Enraged, Silver curses them, spits in the spring, and vows to stove in the blockhouse within the hour.
chapters.cover_description: Long John Silver in his immense blue coat with brass buttons and laced hat, balancing on a crutch as he climbs over the rough log stockade fence on a freezing misty morning, waving a white flag of truce, with the log blockhouse and sandy knoll behind him.

chapters.title: XXI
chapters.summary: After Silver departs, Captain Smollett organizes the seven defenders in the blockhouse with loaded muskets at every loophole. The pirates probe with a harmless volley then rush the north stockade, briefly seizing the house in fierce hand-to-hand fighting before being driven off. The defenders hold the blockhouse but pay dearly, with Joyce dead, Hunter stunned, and the captain wounded, against five pirates fallen.
chapters.cover_description: Pirates swarming over the north stockade palisade in bright sunlight while defenders fire from the log blockhouse loopholes, smoke and musket fire filling the clearing.

chapters.title: XXII
chapters.summary: After repulsing the mutineers, the blockhouse party tends its wounded as Hunter dies and Captain Smollett begins a slow recovery, while Doctor Livesey leaves alone for the woods to find Ben Gunn. Disgusted by the hot, bloody stockade, Jim deserts with biscuit and pistols, treks to the sandy spit, finds Ben Gunn's tiny goatskin coracle by the white rock, and resolves to cut the Hispaniola adrift under cover of foggy night.
chapters.cover_description: A small boy shouldering a tiny goatskin coracle on a dark foggy beach at night, gazing out at the anchored Hispaniola flying the Jolly Roger with a faint cabin light glowing through fog, with a distant pirates' campfire on shore.

chapters.title: XXIII
chapters.summary: Jim paddles Ben Gunn's unmanageable coracle on the ebb tide to the anchored Hispaniola and grabs her hawser, intending to cut her adrift. He waits for a wind puff to slacken the dangerous taut rope and saws through it while overhearing Israel Hands and his red-capped mate drunkenly quarreling and watching the pirates' campfire ashore. Once adrift, he glimpses Hands and the mate locked throat-to-throat in the cabin before schooner and coracle are whirled south through the narrows, where terrified
chapters.cover_description: A tiny round coracle with a boy clinging to the taut anchor hawser of the looming dark schooner Hispaniola at night, rippling black ebb-tide water phosphorescing around the hull.

chapters.title: XXIV
chapters.summary: Adrift in the coracle off the southwest end of Treasure Island, Jim abandons a landing at surf-beaten Haulbowline Head and rides the northward current toward Cape of the Woods, learning to guide the tippy boat without upsetting it while tortured by thirst. He sights the Hispaniola sailing wildly with no hand at the helm, realizes she is unsteered, and paddles hard after her. As the schooner bears down on him, he leaps from his sinking coracle to seize the jib-boom and boards her.
chapters.cover_description: A boy in a tiny coracle leaping upward to grab the jib-boom of the towering schooner Hispaniola as it bears down over him on a bright swell, the swamped coracle sinking beneath his feet.

chapters.title: XXV
chapters.summary: Jim boards the drifting Hispaniola to find its two drunken watchmen, O'Brien dead and Israel Hands wounded, after they fought each other. He fetches brandy and food from the ransacked cabin, declares himself captain, and throws the Jolly Roger overboard. Hands bargains to help sail the ship in exchange for care, and Jim binds his wound and sails for North Inlet to beach her, uneasy at Hands' treacherous watchful smile.
chapters.cover_description: A boy captain hauling down the black Jolly Roger flag from the stern of a bucking schooner while two bloody buccaneers lie fallen on the afterdeck below the swinging boom, bright sunlit sea and Treasure Island coast beyond.

chapters.title: XXVI
chapters.summary: Becalmed off North Inlet, Jim waits with the wounded Israel Hands to beach the Hispaniola, discovering Hands has armed himself with a hidden dirk to kill him. Jim pilots the schooner through the narrow entrance and drives her stem-on ashore, then flees aloft when Hands attacks, killing Hands in the rigging after Hands pins him to the mast with the thrown dirk.
chapters.cover_description: Israel Hands with a bloody dirk in his teeth climbing the mizzen shrouds toward Jim Hawkins perched on the crosstrees, as the beached Hispaniola heels hard over in North Inlet beside a flower-covered wreck.

chapters.title: XXVII
chapters.summary: After killing Israel Hands, Jim frees himself from the mast, dumps O'Brien's body overboard, and secures the canted Hispaniola before wading ashore at sunset. Elated, he hikes back toward the stockade through darkening woods by moonlight to boast of recapturing the ship. Creeping into the dark, snoring blockhouse, he is betrayed by Silver's parrot crying Pieces of eight and captured by Silver and his men who have taken the stockade.
chapters.cover_description: Moonlit night at the silent stockade blockhouse with an immense red ember fire glowing beside it, as a terrified boy Jim Hawkins is seized in the dark doorway while Long John Silver on his crutch shouts and his green parrot on his shoulder shrieks Pieces of eight by torchlight.

chapters.title: XXVIII
chapters.summary: Jim returns to the blockhouse to find it held by Silver's pirates and his friends gone, and learns from Silver that Livesey traded the stores and blockhouse after the Hispaniola vanished. Jim defiantly confesses to spying, cutting the ship adrift, and killing its guards, offering to speak for them at trial, which provokes the men but makes Silver protect him as captain. After the crew leaves for a forecastle council to depose him, Silver privately bargains with Jim to save each other and reveals
chapters.cover_description: Torch-lit interior of the log blockhouse at night, Long John Silver seated across a brandy cask smoking his pipe with his green parrot on his shoulder, staring down a defiant boy with his back against the log wall while five rough pirates glare from the shadows.

chapters.title: XXIX
chapters.summary: The mutineers in council present Long John Silver with the Black Spot marked Deposed, cut sacrilegiously from a Bible. Silver demands his right to answer their four charges of bungling, freeing enemies, refusing attack, and protecting Jim, then reverses the mutiny by producing Flint's treasure chart and is re-elected captain, leaving Jim awake to ponder Silver's double game for survival.
chapters.cover_description: Inside a dark log blockhouse at night, one-legged Long John Silver holds up a torch to examine a small blackened circle of paper cut from a Bible, while young Jim Hawkins watches and mutineers crowd in the doorway, with Flint's yellow treasure chart with red crosses lying on the floor.

chapters.title: XXX
chapters.summary: Doctor Livesey visits the blockhouse at dawn to tend the sick pirates and is shocked to find Jim Hawkins held prisoner by Silver. Silver secures Jim's parole to speak with the doctor through the stockade, then begs Livesey for mercy for himself and the boy. Jim refuses to break his word and escape, but confesses he has retaken the ship in North Inlet, and Livesey leaves with cryptic warnings and a promise to help Silver if he keeps Jim safe.
chapters.cover_description: Doctor Livesey standing up to his knees in morning mist outside the log blockhouse stockade at dawn, facing Long John Silver on his crutch with young Jim Hawkins beside him, pirates watching from inside.

chapters.title: XXXI
chapters.summary: Silver privately pledges to stick with Jim through the treasure hunt to save their necks, then restores the pirates' morale over breakfast by promising Jim as hostage and success with the boats. Roped to Silver, Jim marches with the armed party across the anchorage and up the island, where they find a compass-laid skeleton that Silver calls Flint's pointer, striking terror into the men.
chapters.cover_description: A human skeleton laid perfectly straight under a pine with hands raised like a diver pointing toward Skeleton Island, while a crutch-using cook with a parrot on his shoulder takes a compass bearing and roped boy and fearful pirates gather around.

chapters.title: XXXII
chapters.summary: The treasure party rests on the brow overlooking the island while Silver takes bearings to the three tall trees, then freezes in terror when Flint's song and a wail for rum echo from the woods. Silver rallies them with the claim of an echo and that it is Ben Gunn, and they hurry across the hot summit to the giant third tree, only to find the cache long-emptied with a broken pick and Walrus cases and the seven hundred thousand pounds gone.
chapters.cover_description: A giant red-trunked pine towering over a sun-baked plateau, its wide shadow falling on a grass-grown rifled pit littered with a broken pick shaft and staved packing-case boards branded WALRUS, while a one-legged cook on a crutch and ragged pirates stare in disbelief.

chapters.title: XXXIII
chapters.summary: The treasure pit is found empty, sparking a standoff between Silver and Jim and the furious mutineers until the doctor, Gray, and Ben Gunn ambush the mutineers from the thicket. The doctor explains Ben Gunn had long ago found and hidden Flint's treasure in his cave and traded the useless chart to lure the mutineers into a trap. The party recovers the drifting Hispaniola, reunites at the treasure-filled cave, and celebrates with supper despite the squire's condemnation of Silver.
chapters.cover_description: Inside a large firelit island cave, great heaps of gold coins and stacked bars of gold glitter in the firelight while exhausted seamen share supper around a blaze — Flint's long-sought treasure finally found.

chapters.title: XXXIV
chapters.summary: After days of hauling Flint's vast hoard from the cave to the Hispaniola, the crew hears the marooned mutineers raving below and holds a council to desert them with stores on the island. They sail from North Inlet past the kneeling castaways, reach a Spanish American port where Silver escapes with a sack of guineas, and return to Bristol to divide the treasure and settle into new lives while Jim remains haunted by the island.
chapters.cover_description: The Hispaniola under full sail pulling away from Treasure Island while three marooned mutineers kneel together on a narrow sand spit with arms raised in supplication, one firing a musket over the deck as the island sinks into the blue sea.
